messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — SLO breach detected on redwood-hosting-prod: p99 generation latency > 2s for 5m. Affected route: /v1/streaming/generate. Paging oncall: @oncall-ml
oncall-ml: acknowledged. I’m looking. p95 and p99 dashboards?
sre-alyssa: pulling dashboards now. p95 is 600ms but p99 jumped to 2.5s. Streaming stall rate spiked to 3.8% (baseline <0.2%).
eng-runtime: any recent deploys / config changes? :thinking_face:
oncall-ml: no deploys in last 30m. autoscaler flapping? infra-lead: checking node health in gpu-pool-12
infra-lead: seeing ECC errors on gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-14, hardware-reported thermal events on gpu-node-12. Kernel logs show repeated machine-check warnings.
eng-oncall: logs:
```
[2026-03-14T02:12:05Z] GPU ECC error: device 0000:65:00.0 uncorrectable
[2026-03-14T02:12:06Z] GPU thermal event: temp=95C throttle
[2026-03-14T02:12:07Z] nv_peer_mem: peer error
```
sre-alyssa: correlating request traces -> tail requests hitting nodes with degraded GPUs are showing stalls during KV cache fetch (large token spans). p99 tokens/sec drops to ~0.1 for affected shards.
oncall-ml: immediate mitigation options: 1) route traffic away from gpu-pool-12 to other pools, 2) fallback to smaller model variant, 3) drain affected nodes. Which order?
eng-runtime: do 1 + 2 quickly. Update routing policy to avoid pool first; we can flip routing within ~30s. Then start draining suspect nodes for evacuation.
incident-bot: action started: set-routing policy updated to prefer gpu-pool-03,gpu-pool-07 over gpu-pool-12. Rolling update id: ru-20260314-01
eng-runtime: initiating traffic switch now. :mega:
support-miguel: note — customer-visible errors in support queue referencing "slow responses" for real-time agents. Filed 3 tickets in last 15m.
product-ops: we should prep a short status message for customers if impact persists beyond 30m. cs-jane can you prepare a blurb?
cs-jane: on it, draft in #support-digest and will share.
oncall-ml: starting `kubectl drain` on gpu-node-12. Command used:
```
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```
eng-oncall: watch out for pods pinned to GPUs with local state (we'll have short failovers). Also reduce max_concurrency for streaming routes to 2 while routing moves.
eng-runtime: changed service config: `max_concurrency: 2` for /v1/streaming/generate. Deploying config patch.
incident-bot: deploy-bot: config patch applied by eng-runtime. Build: b-3192. Rolling restarts started.
sre-alyssa: metrics after routing change (30s post): p95 420ms, p99 1.1s, streaming-stall 0.9%. Improvement but still above SLO for p99.
infra-lead: drain completed for gpu-node-12, node in `drained` state. Marking for maintenance and vendor escalation. Attaching ECC logs.
infra-lead: opening ticket with hardware vendor now (ref HW-20260314-07). ETA for replacement 72h, but vendor agreed to on-site triage.
eng-runtime: we'll keep fallback active and autoscale capacity in healthy pools. Also enabling prefix KV cache warmup to reduce cold-stream stalls.
eng-oncall: FYI, one legacy customer route still pinned to gpu-pool-12 due to affinity. Doing a manual override.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: override applied. All traffic off gpu-pool-12.
sre-alyssa: p99 now 880ms; p95 390ms; streaming stall 0.3% — back within SLO for most customers. Continue monitoring.
support-miguel: sending CS note to affected customers with status. Template:
```
We're investigating intermittent high latency for streaming responses. We've rerouted traffic and applied mitigations. No data loss. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline.
```
product-ops: good. Add expected next update in 60m.
oncall-ml: handing off to offshift oncall @eng-oncall for 22:00 - please continue monitoring and confirm stable. :wave:
eng-oncall: taking handoff. I have runbooks and will escalate to infra-lead if metrics degrade again.
infra-lead: next steps: 1) schedule hardware replacement for gpu-node-12/14, 2) run full ECC/thermal stress tests on spare nodes, 3) review cooling and rack airflow, 4) add node-level auto-evacuation when ECC thresholds exceed X/min.
sre-alyssa: postmortem owners: eng-runtime + infra. Initial RCA hypothesis: intermittent ECC and thermal faults causing GPU stalls -> degraded kernel-level ops -> request stalls at tail. Suspected hardware degradation on 2 nodes in same rack causing localized p99 tail spikes.
eng-runtime: will produce remediation plan: node fencing thresholds, routing failover automation, and safer fallback ordering. ETA for plan: EOD.
incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity set: Sev3. Incident created: 1978000000. Timeline notes attached.
cs-jane: posted CS update. Will coordinate with product-ops for follow-up.
support-miguel: closing customer-facing tickets after confirm. :white_check_mark:
eng-oncall: continuing 1h of heightened monitoring, will update if regressions. If p99 > 1.5s for 5m, page infra-lead and eng-runtime.
infra-lead: acknowledged. Preparing hardware escalation pack and logs.
eng-runtime: adding runbook entry for thermal+ECC thresholds to avoid manual triage next time.
sre-alyssa: thanks everyone — great coordination. We'll capture full timeline and actions for the postmortem.
eng-oncall: :thumbsup:
